blocks.title: What it is meant to be

body.en: A conventional UUID is 128 bits that point at an object. The W5D UUID is described as a long-form identifier, possibly 8 to 16 MB, whose embedded structure turns the identifier from a pointer into a genome.

blocks.title: What exists, and what does not

rows.en: A research direction described in a founder declaration. No specification is published.
No specification, reference implementation or storage and transfer measurements are published.

body.en: An identifier of 8 to 16 MB has storage, transfer, indexing and verification costs that have not been measured. It is unrelated to the standard UUID formats in RFC 9562 and must not be used where a 16-byte UUID is expected.
